title: Neon Genesis Evangelion
wiki_lead:
Neon Genesis Evangelion (Japanese: 新世紀エヴァンゲリオン, Hepburn: Shin Seiki Evangerion; lit. 'New Century Evangelion' in Japanese and lit. 'New Beginning Gospel' in Greek), also known as simply Evangelion or Eva, is a Japanese anime television series produced by Gainax and Tatsunoko Production, and directed by Hideaki Anno. It was broadcast on TV Tokyo and its affiliates from October 1995 to March 1996. The story, set in 2015, fifteen years after a worldwide cataclysm in the futuristic fortified city of Tokyo-3, follows Shinji Ikari, a teenage boy who is recruited by his father Gendo Ikari to the mysterious organization Nerv. Shinji is tasked to pilot an Evangelion, a giant biomechanical mecha, to fight and destroy beings known as Angels.
The series has been described as a deconstruction of the mecha genre; it delves into the experiences, emotions, and mental health of the Evangelion pilots and Nerv members as they are called upon to understand the ultimate cause of events and the motives behind human action. The series features archetypal imagery derived from Shinto cosmology and mystical Judeo-Christian religions and traditions, including Midrashic tales and Kabbalah. The psychoanalytic accounts of human behavior put forward by Sigmund Freud and Carl Jung are also prominently featured.
Neon Genesis Evangelion received acclaim from critics and audiences and is regarded as one of the greatest animated series of all time; however, its final two episodes drew controversy, as many viewers found the ending confusing and abstract. Gainax attributed the episodes' abstract style both to the severe time constraints imposed by the production schedule and to Anno's deliberate artistic choice. In 1997, Gainax released a remake of the last two episodes in the feature film The End of Evangelion, written and co-directed by Anno. A series of four films, Rebuild of Evangelion, retelling the events of the series with different plot elements and a new ending, were released between 2007 and 2021. Evangelion has had a profound influence on the anime industry and influenced numerous future works. Films, manga, home video releases, and other products in the franchise have achieved record sales in Japanese markets and strong sales in overseas markets, with related goods earning over ¥150 billion by 2007 and Evangelion pachinko machines generating ¥700 billion by 2015.

Plot

In 2015, 15 years after a global cataclysm known as the Second Impact, teenager Shinji Ikari is summoned to the futuristic city of Tokyo-3 by his estranged father Gendo Ikari, who is the director of the special paramilitary organization Nerv. Shinji witnesses United Nations forces battling a giant creature named Sachiel, one of a race of monstrous beings known as Angels whose awakening was foretold in the Dead Sea Scrolls. The Japanese title Shin Seiki Evangelion translates to "New Century Evangelion" or "Gospel of the New Century," while the English title Neon Genesis Evangelion derives from Greek roots: "neon" meaning "new," "genesis" meaning "origin" or "birth," and "Evangelion" from "euangelion" meaning "good news" or "gospel," yielding interpretations such as "Gospel of the New Beginning" or "New Genesis Gospel." This title encapsulates the series' core themes of apocalypse, existential struggle, and the possibility of renewal or rebirth for humanity. Set in the post-apocalyptic year 2015, fifteen years after the global cataclysm known as the Second Impact that killed half of humanity, the story follows 14-year-old Shinji Ikari, who is conscripted by his estranged father Gendo to pilot Evangelion Unit-01, a massive bio-mechanical humanoid piloted by select teenagers known as Children, for the organization NERV in battles against mysterious gigantic invaders known as Angels possessing protective A.T. Fields, the offspring of Adam seeking to reunite with Lilith, threatening Tokyo-3. Shinji, joined by fellow Children pilots Rei Ayanami and the competitive Asuka Langley Soryu, navigates not only these existential threats but also severe psychological distress, fractured familial bonds, and revelations about human evolution tied to ancient lore and the machinations of NERV's overseers and the cabal SEELE. The series foregrounds introspective character studies and themes of depression, isolation, and the hedgehog's dilemma âreflecting Anno's personal battles with clinical depression during productionâover escapist action, earning acclaim for its raw emotional authenticity while subverting mecha genre conventions that typically glorify youthful heroism and seamless teamwork. Neon Genesis Evangelion marked a commercial triumph, boosting Gainax's fortunes amid financial woes and catalyzing the 1990s anime boom through high viewership, soundtrack sales topping Japanese charts, and a franchise that has amassed over $16 billion in revenue from films, merchandise, and spin-offs. Its finale's abstract introspection provoked initial fan backlash for abandoning plot resolution, leading to the 1997 film The End of Evangelion as a violent denouement, yet the work's enduring influence persists in reshaping anime toward psychological depth and multimedia empires.
